Buffalo's Socrata permit items are filtered views with no readable parent dataset, and Columbus/Jacksonville surfaced no permit feed in catalog or ArcGIS search, so the run audited Los Angeles next and it passed. (1) Dataset 'Building and Safety - Building Permits Issued from 2020 to Present (N)' (City of Los Angeles, Socrata pi9x-tg5x; dataset owner 'Building and Safety OpenData' — LADBS): 421,919 rows all-time; the dataset's own metadata states Committed Update Frequency 'Weekly' and Automated 'Yes'; rowsUpdatedAt 2026-11-02T17:09:15Z; per-row refresh_time is 2026-11-01 on every row (a full weekly reload); max issue_date 2026-10-31. (2) VOLUME STABILITY measured by issue month: 4,492–6,160 permits/month across 2024–2026 with no collapse (Sep 2026: 5,928; Oct 2026: 6,160); weekday issuance runs ~270–310/day through Oct 30, 2026. (3) Identity measured on the trailing-12-month window (issue_date >= 2025-11-06): 63,778 rows = 63,778 distinct permit_nbr, one row per permit, no collapsing. (4) Coverage is City of Los Angeles building permits only: permit_group is 'Building' on 100% of all-time rows — LADBS publishes its electrical and mechanical (plumbing/HVAC/fire sprinkler/elevator) permits in separate datasets, which are NOT in this feed (printed on the hub; the Raleigh treatment). Los Angeles County's other cities publish separately. (5) The 39-column schema publishes NO contractor, applicant, or owner name field at all, so contractor_name stays NULL, never inferred (the SF/Boston treatment). coverage_note: Building permits issued by the City of Los Angeles (Department of Building and Safety) only. Los Angeles County's other cities issue their own permits and are not in this feed; LADBS electrical and mechanical permits are published in separate city datasets and are not in this report either.

dedupe_rule.definition: One published permit = one permit_nbr in the City of Los Angeles LADBS building-permits dataset. The dataset's grain is one row per issued building permit: no collapsing applies or is needed.
dedupe_rule.measurement: Trailing-12-month window (issue_date >= 2025-11-06), measured 2026-11-06: 63,778 rows = 63,778 distinct permit_nbr, 0 duplicates, 0 nulls. The pipeline's in-batch duplicate gate and the (county_id, source_record_id) upsert key guard every future pull.

field_map.address: primary_address, as published (whitespace collapsed; all-caps values title-cased). Present on 63,777 of 63,778 window permits.
field_map.application_date: submitted_date (the date the application was submitted; present on 37,094 of 63,778 window permits — the city's express/e-permits carry no submitted date, so it stays NULL there).
field_map.category: permit_sub_type, the city's own building class: '1 or 2 Family Dwelling' (48,224 window permits) and 'Apartment' (7,867) = residential; 'Commercial' (6,365) = commercial; the grading classes 'Onsite' (1,046) and 'Offsite' (276) state no building class and stay NULL.
field_map.contractor_rule: The dataset publishes no contractor, applicant, or owner name field at all (full 39-column schema verified 2026-11-06), so contractor_name stays NULL, never inferred.
field_map.issue_date: issue_date. The window is defined on it: a record enters this report when LADBS records an issue date.
field_map.permit_number: permit_nbr (unique in the window, see dedupe_rule). Supplemental permits carry their own permit numbers and are counted as the separate permits the city issued (the Chicago/NYC treatment).
field_map.permit_type: permit_type, LADBS's own permit family naming (Bldg-Alter/Repair, Bldg-Addition, Bldg-New, Grading, Swimming-Pool/Spa, Nonbldg-New, Bldg-Demolition, Sign, Nonbldg-Alter/Repair, Nonbldg-Addition, Nonbldg-Demolition).
field_map.project_description: work_desc, the permit's published scope-of-work text, as reported (whitespace collapsed).
field_map.status: status_desc, mapped through status_map; the verbatim source value is kept in status_source. Window statuses: Issued 38,340 / Permit Finaled 23,232 / CofO Issued 1,563 / CofO in Progress 326 / Permit Closed 179 / CofC Issued 48 / the rest are single- and double-digit process states — every window record carries an issue date, so post-issuance states stay in the population (the Raleigh treatment).
field_map.valuation: valuation (a text column of plain dollar figures), stored and published as reported. Measured on the full window (2026-11-06, full audit pull): stated on 63,774 of 63,778 permits (4 null); 3,670 at $0 and only 37 at $1; median positive value $8,000; window total $9,462,221,760.33. No stamp pathology: ZERO non-round values of $1M or more repeat at different addresses (the Seattle disease is absent); repeated large values are round applicant budgets only ($1,000,000 x79 — the Boston signature). The largest permit ($1,966,896,355, the LAX Terminal 5 rebuild-and-addition at 500 World Way) appears exactly once — 20.8% of the total, a real flagship airport project whose description prints alongside (the Chicago shape); the same project's foundation permit states its own $333,103,645, a different figure, not a restatement. VALUES PUBLISH; the DB window sum must reproduce the source-side total, and September 2026 must match the source exactly (5,928 permits).

history_range: issue_date 2020 onward in this dataset (the city publishes pre-2020 permits in sibling datasets); we backfill the trailing 12 months only (site rule).
license: City of Los Angeles open-data terms (portal standard); attribution: City of Los Angeles, California
rate_limit: Socrata anonymous tier; paged at 5,000 rows/request with the adapter's 0.4s pacing.
source_name: City of Los Angeles open data — Building Permits Issued (LADBS)
terms_status: verified-open-2026-11-06: the City of Los Angeles publishes this dataset on its open-data portal (data.lacity.org) for public reuse under the portal's standard terms; dataset owner is the Department of Building and Safety ('Building and Safety OpenData'); figures are published 'as reported by the City of Los Angeles' with attribution; no endorsement is implied.
update_cadence: Weekly full reload, per the dataset's own metadata ('Committed Update Frequency: Weekly', 'Automated? Yes'); MEASURED 2026-11-06: rowsUpdatedAt 2026-11-02T17:09:15Z and per-row refresh_time 2026-11-01 on all rows, with permits issued through 2026-10-31 — a roughly one-week issuance lag, shown honestly in the page stamps. Freshness (gate 5) is measured as the dataset's rowsUpdatedAt under a 240h threshold, sized to the source's own weekly cadence (the Tier-2 treatment); the first nightly refresh runs will confirm the reload rhythm.
watermark_field: issue_date + permit_nbr — refresh re-pulls by the issue_date watermark and upserts.
